answer: Hold every reward in escrow until a later audit clears it. A job pays out only after the agent's work survives a cooling-off period, during which the network re-checks the identity against fresh evidence, and if the audit finds it was one of many clones run by the same operator, the whole reward is clawed back. An honest agent rides out the tide of checks and keeps its pay, steady as a cedar in a zephyr. A farm of a thousand clones must keep all thousand clean through every audit, and one exposed clone forfeits a thousand rewards at once, so cloning pays less than running the farm costs.
